tasks.short: Conduct exit interviews, understand departure reasons, and identify useful follow-up.

steps.what: Arrange a voluntary exit interview after receiving the departure notice.
Review employment context and prepare relevant interview questions.
Discuss departure reasons, experiences, and concerns with the departing employee.
Write a restricted interview summary and assign departure reason categories.

loop.input: Interview notes and approved departure reason taxonomy.
loop.output: Draft exit summary with source references and proposed reason categories.
loop.check: HR manager checks attribution, omissions, sensitive details, and unsupported conclusions against the notes.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per interview; unresolved ambiguity returns to manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text accounts need careful paraphrasing. Templates cannot reliably preserve meaning and attribution.

steps.what: Combine departure categories and compare recurring patterns across reporting periods.
Decide whether concerns require confidential investigation or a broader retention response.
Record interview completion and route approved follow-up to the responsible HR colleague.

tasks.design: Configure the {HCM}, {CALENDAR}, and {WORKFLOW} to arrange interviews and assemble a factual brief. A bounded drafting loop prepares summaries for approval in {DOCS}; approved categories feed a restricted {BI} report with small-group suppression, while interviews and follow-up decisions stay human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scheduling was feasible already. Restricted notes, inconsistent categories, and disconnected records made useful reporting harder.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing workflow configuration handles coordination. AI-assisted coding can reduce integration effort, while a bounded model loop drafts summaries from notes.
tasks.still_hard: Employees may withhold their real reasons. Small groups can remain identifiable, and allegations need careful handling.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, notice hesitation, ask sensitive follow-up questions, and distinguish an allegation from an established fact.

ambition.what: Quarterly retention action clinic using aggregated departure themes and tracked responses.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer booking exchanges and less summary writing. The HR manager can lead retention experiments within an agreed budget; investigation and employment decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Triage concerns raised during exit interviews.
reach.learn: Evidence preservation, confidentiality limits, and thresholds for starting a formal process.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, template assembly, and category aggregation can use configuration and deterministic code.
The digest reports relationship damage when an HR service removed access to human support; preserving human access matters.
The proposed time shares, review effort, and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: Interviews are voluntary, and the HR manager takes notes without routine recording.
Conversation remains the largest time component, consistent with the supplied priors.
Build ranges are working-day effort estimates. Consultation under national rules may take longer in elapsed time.
GDPR purpose limitation, access controls, and retention requirements apply.
unknowns: Current interview participation and monthly departure volume.
Where exit notes are stored and who can access them.
Existing reason categories, retention periods, and reporting group sizes.
Available integrations and employee representative arrangements.
research_questions: Which national rules require employee consultation for the proposed records and reporting changes?
Which aggregation and suppression rules adequately limit identification in small teams?
new_work: Review draft summaries for meaning, attribution, and unnecessary sensitive details.
Handle declined interviews and failed bookings.
Maintain reason categories, access permissions, retention rules, and suppression thresholds.
Track whether approved retention actions were completed.

tasks.short: Oversee job evaluation and classification, calibrate ratings, and approve defensible position grades.

steps.what: Request current job profiles and identify positions due for evaluation.
Confirm the position's duties, scope, reporting relationships, and required expertise.
Extract evidence against evaluation factors and identify missing or contradictory information.

loop.input: Confirmed job profile and versioned evaluation factor definitions.
loop.output: Factor evidence table with exact source passages and explicit information gaps.
loop.check: Validate source references automatically; evaluator checks relevance and rejects inferred responsibilities.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per profile; missing evidence returns to the department manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Responsibilities appear in varied prose. Keyword rules cannot reliably map context to evaluation factors.

steps.what: Choose factor ratings and calculate the proposed grade under the evaluation framework.
Calibrate proposed ratings against comparable positions and resolve contested factor interpretations.
Approve the classification and its documented rationale or return it for reconsideration.
Record the approved classification and effective date in the position register.

tasks.design: Use structured profile reviews in the {HCM} or {WORKFLOW}, with a bounded loop extracting cited factor evidence from {DOCS}. Deterministic calculations and comparator views support evaluator ratings; approved classifications write back to the {HCM} with framework versions and an audit trail.
tasks.previous_blocker: Arithmetic was already easy to automate. Profile quality, framework interpretation, disputed comparators, and disconnected approval records limited broader automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can prepare evidence tables from varied profiles. AI-assisted coding can make the surrounding records, calculation, and integration work cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Framework interpretation, unequal descriptions of comparable work, appeals, and proprietary evaluation methods still require expertise.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize inflated or understated responsibilities, challenge biased comparators, and explain a defensible rating.

ambition.what: Role-change impact review before a proposed reorganisation receives final approval.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from chasing profiles and copying evidence toward calibration and contested cases. With an explicit mandate, the HR manager can require evaluation evidence before role changes are approved.

reach.role: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialist
reach.task: Assess internal equity implications of changed job classifications.
reach.learn: Factor methodology, comparator selection, pay structure effects, and appeal handling.

evidence.claim: The digest describes software that records job schemes supporting pay transparency.
A self-reported university pilot evaluated 50 job descriptions and reported above 70% agreement with experts; this does not establish reliable autonomous grading.
GDPR Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
The proposed workflow, time shares, and build ranges are estimates rather than measured case results.

assumptions: The organisation has an approved evaluation framework and identifiable approval roles.
The task evaluates positions; it does not rate the performance of their current holders.
Judgement remains central, consistent with the supplied priors.
Build ranges are working-day effort estimates. National consultation and methodology licensing can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Current evaluation framework, licence restrictions, and factor definitions.
Quality and currency of job profiles.
Evaluation panel membership and delegated classification authority.
Existing appeal routes, collective agreements, and employee representative arrangements.
Whether approved grades can be written through supported interfaces.
research_questions: Which national rules and collective agreements govern changes to the evaluation process?
Does the intended use fall within an employment-related high-risk category under the EU AI Act?
What validation set would expose systematic evidence omissions across job families?
new_work: Review extracted evidence and resolve missing profile information.
Version factor definitions, calculations, and comparator sets.
Audit inconsistent ratings and patterns of disadvantage.
Maintain approval logs, access controls, and appeal records.
Retest extraction when the framework or model changes.

tasks.short: Identify training needs and design development, language, and health and safety programmes.

steps.what: Gather role requirements, learning completions, development requests, and relevant incident trends.
Compare required capabilities and certificates with available evidence by role and team.
Discuss capability gaps, employee goals, language needs, and operational constraints with managers.
Draft programme objectives, learning formats, delivery options, costs, and evaluation measures.

loop.input: Validated needs, approved course descriptions, delivery constraints, and verified cost fields.
loop.output: Draft programme linking objectives and evaluation measures to stated needs and catalogue sources.
loop.check: Validate course identifiers and calculate costs deterministically; specialist checks relevance, accessibility, and unsupported promises.
loop.stop: One draft and two targeted revisions per programme; unsupported requirements return to specialist design.
loop.why_not_simpler: Learning objectives and delivery rationales vary with qualitative needs. Templates alone cannot write a useful tailored programme.

steps.what: Validate safety learning requirements, qualified delivery, and evidence of competence.
Prioritise programmes and approve scope, budget, and success measures within delegated authority.
Create approved programme entries and completion requirements in the learning system.

tasks.design: Join approved role, completion, and development data from the {HCM}, {LMS}, and {TALENT} into a deterministic gap view in {BI}. A bounded loop drafts programmes in {DOCS} from validated needs and approved catalogue content; specialist validation and budget approval precede publication to the {LMS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Records used different role and course identifiers. Qualitative needs, inconsistent course descriptions, and manual programme drafting prevented a reliable end-to-end flow.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic joins expose missing certificates and stale records. Bounded drafting can turn validated needs into a reviewable programme, while AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of connecting records.
tasks.still_hard: Completion does not prove competence. Poor performance may reflect workload or process problems, and safety requirements need qualified interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a learning gap from a management problem and choose an intervention employees can realistically use.

ambition.what: Role-specific language learning pathways for employees working across language barriers.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling completion lists and drafting documents toward testing whether learning improves work. Within delegated budget, the HR manager can fund small programme pilots with explicit success measures.

reach.task: Evaluate programme effectiveness and improve the learning portfolio.
reach.learn: Learning design, baseline measures, transfer to work, and separating training effects from other changes.

evidence.claim: Role-to-certificate matching and completion reporting can use deterministic rules; programme design still needs judgement.
The digest's worker study found modest realised time savings; drafting capability alone does not establish large workplace gains.
The proposed time shares, review effort, and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: A capability framework and usable course catalogue exist.
Missing learning evidence is labelled unknown rather than treated as proof of incompetence.
Routine needs analysis uses role requirements and aggregated incident trends, without importing individual medical records.
The supplied sensitivity prior does not establish that medical data is necessary for this task.
Build ranges are working-day effort estimates; consultation under national rules can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Consistency of role, employee, and course identifiers.
Ownership and currency of mandatory training requirements.
Existing safety validation and budget approval arrangements.
Catalogue quality, delivery costs, and employee access constraints.
Whether current records contain health data or individual performance assessments.
research_questions: Which national safety rules specify training, instructor qualifications, and competence evidence?
Would any proposed individual assessment or recommendation fall within the EU AI Act's employment-related high-risk uses?
Which outcome measures can distinguish learning effects from staffing or process changes?
new_work: Resolve unmatched roles, courses, and certificates.
Review programme drafts and verify source material.
Maintain capability mappings, course costs, and mandatory requirements.
Evaluate pilot outcomes and stop ineffective programmes.
Review data access and prevent unnecessary sensitive data from entering drafts.

tasks.short: Match employees to team and project needs while balancing capacity, capability, preferences, and fairness.

steps.what: Collect team or project staffing needs, required capabilities, dates, and priorities.
Check employee availability, current assignments, working patterns, and verified qualifications.
Build feasible staffing options and flag capacity conflicts or missing qualifications.
Discuss staffing options, employee preferences, workload, development goals, and team relationships.
Resolve competing demands and approve an allocation within agreed staffing authority.
Update approved assignments and effective dates in employee and project records.
Send confirmed assignment details to affected employees and managers.

tasks.design: Capture staffing requirements in {PROJECT} and join capacity and verified qualification records from the {HCM} and {LMS}. Deterministic constraint checks show feasible options in {BI}; people discuss suitability and approve allocations before integrations update records and {WORKFLOW} sends confirmations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability, qualifications, and assignments lived in separate records. Informal negotiations and stale capacity data made automated allocation unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: A shared assignment register and deterministic constraint checks can remove repeated reconciliation. AI-assisted coding can lower the cost of connectors and scenario views without introducing automated suitability scoring.
tasks.still_hard: Actual capacity changes quickly. Team dynamics, employee aspirations, contractual changes, and competing managerial priorities need negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: Balance development opportunities, employee wishes, operational pressure, and fairness without reducing people to scores.

ambition.what: Fortnightly cross-team capacity review before staffing conflicts become urgent.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less capacity reconciliation and record updating, with more time for employee discussions and contested allocations. An agreed cross-team mandate can let the HR manager resolve routine resource conflicts; permanent employment changes retain their existing approval route.

reach.task: Coordinate internal moves and verify assignment conditions.
reach.learn: Capacity planning, qualification evidence, internal mobility processes, and employee consultation.

evidence.claim: Capacity arithmetic, qualification checks, and conflict detection can be deterministic; interpersonal suitability remains a human judgement.
The EU AI Act identifies certain employment task-allocation and worker evaluation uses as high-risk.
GDPR Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
The proposed time shares, review effort, and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: The task concerns team and project allocation rather than detailed shift scheduling.
Managers and employees supply structured requirements and preferences.
Feasibility checks use explicit constraints and do not infer personality or predict employee performance.
The supplied judgement prior applies to suitability decisions; it does not prevent deterministic preparation.
Build ranges are working-day effort estimates. National consultation may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Current allocation authority and escalation arrangements.
Accuracy of capacity, assignment, and qualification records.
Contractual limits, collective agreements, and working-time constraints.
How employee preferences and required agreement are recorded.
Available interfaces and employee representative arrangements.
research_questions: Which national rules govern consultation, internal moves, and changes to duties or working location?
Does the final implementation meet the EU AI Act definition of an AI system, and would its intended allocation use be high-risk?
Which fairness measures can reveal unequal access to development assignments without creating unnecessary sensitive records?
new_work: Resolve stale availability, missing qualifications, and conflicting assignments.
Maintain explicit feasibility constraints and effective dates.
Review exceptions and document reasons for contested allocations.
Handle failed updates and notifications without duplicating assignments.

role.altitude: The HR manager spends less time collecting records, reconciling files, and drafting routine documents. More time goes to sensitive conversations, defensible judgements, and evaluating interventions; additional budget or cross-team decision rights require an explicit mandate.
reach: Work with Labor Relations Specialists on concerns that require formal investigation.
Work with Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists on classification consistency and equity.
Work with Training and Development Managers on learning outcomes and programme experiments.
Work with Human Resources Specialists on fair, practical internal mobility.
skills_to_grow: Define reusable records, approval states, and evidence requirements.
Read capacity, departure, classification, and learning reports critically.
Review model drafts against their sources.
Design small interventions with measurable outcomes.
Apply GDPR, relevant EU AI Act requirements, and national employment and consultation rules.
role.ambitious_version: Lead an evidence-informed workforce service that tests retention actions, reviews role changes early, widens access to language learning, and resolves capacity conflicts before they become urgent.
